data.body:
LIVE VERIFICATION COMPLETE — J10 is confirmed NON-REGRESSIVE against a real Jira Data Center.

GitHub Actions run 30623000498, job 'jira DC harness smoke', on main at db2b0dc14 (J10's commit).

    RESULT: 2 failed, 12 passed, 1 error
    PRIOR (run 30604756524, pre-J10): 2 failed, 12 passed, 1 error

IDENTICAL. All three predictions I stated IN ADVANCE held:

 1. The 12 previously-passing live tests STILL PASS. That was the whole point of this run: the
    translation went in at _with_connection_retry, the single choke point EVERY DC transport method
    routes through, so a regression there would have hit all twelve — and no unit test exercises the
    real retry path against a real server. It did not regress.
 2. The two writing tests still fail, AND I VERIFIED THE CAUSE rather than inferring it from an
    identical failure count:
        reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute 'set_entity_property'
    Same cause as before, which is what should happen: J10 translated JIRAError, and a MISSING
    ATTRIBUTE raises AttributeError, not JIRAError, so translation cannot and should not mask it.
    'Two failed both times' would have been a weak inference; the error string is the evidence.
 3. The PAT-cap error recurred exactly as predicted — see [rebar:f391-806b-938f-45d8].

WHAT THIS BUYS: J10 was closed on unit evidence alone (1660 tests, 11 held-out contract tests), which
in this epic has repeatedly meant nothing. It is now live-verified. And the remaining live failure is
cleanly attributable to J9's missing members rather than to anything J10 did — which is exactly the
separation the split was meant to produce.
